text:
maya: Heads-up: saw a 'residency double-count' spike during compaction on shard-7. Eviction logs show the same prefix being marked evicted and handed off concurrently. Anyone seen this?

lia: I saw something similar once but couldn't repro. Can you paste the logs + shard id + sequence?

maya: shard=7, prefix=org/123/conv/tx. Timeline looks like: compaction triggered -> eviction scan -> slab compactor moved entries -> handoff ack. Logs snippet: ```[evict] prefix=org/123/conv/tx evicting id=0xabc state=RESIDENT -> EVICTING
[handoff] prefix=org/123/conv/tx new_owner=shard-9 ack=ok
[evict] complete but residency_count=2
```

kevin: hmm, that reads like compactor writes new_owner then eviction finalizer clears residency in the old owner, but ordering allows both to think they hold a resident. Race between handoff commit and eviction completion.

sarah: iirc our handoff path assumes eviction is finalizer. Compactor should either wait for no in-flight reads or take a transfer lease. Current fast-path does owner_set -> clear_resid which is racy under compaction.

arjun: low friction fix: add a transient 'handoff-reserved' bit/counter on residency entries. Protocol: compactor increments reserved, sets new_owner, waits for resident_count==reserved+1 (or drain), then decrements reserved and lets old owner evict. Evict path checks reserved and defers finalization while reserved>0. Cheap and read path unchanged.

kevin: alternate: owner+epoch token. Handoff creates new (owner,epoch). Eviction only decrements if epoch matches. Simple CAS semantics: ```struct ResEntry { owner u64; epoch u64; count u32; } // CAS on (owner,epoch)``` This avoids extra counters but touches hot metadata.

lia: what's the perf hit? reads are super hot; we can't add heavy CAS on read path.

sarah: agreed — try to keep read path single load + atomic increment. Both proposals avoid touching that on reads. Epoch approach adds a compare on handoff path only if implemented correctly.

maya: :thinking_face: what about aborted compactions? If compactor crashes after marking reserved/new_owner, prefix can get stuck.

arjun: we can piggyback on lease-manager. Compactor obtains a short transfer lease; if it dies lease expires and scavenger clears reserved/new_owner. TTL fallback is ok.

kevin: or keep it simpler: reserved counter decays (scavenger decrements) if not confirmed within N seconds and we emit an aborted_handoff metric. That gives visibility.

lia: sounds pragmatic. We'll need a stress harness to simulate compactor crash and race with eviction. Unit tests won't catch timing.

sarah: agree. Add metrics: handoff_reserves, aborted_handoffs, handoff_latency. Also a flag to enable the new handoff-reserve behavior behind feature flag.

maya: I'll run a fuzz stress for compactor + eviction with canary. If stable we open an RFC for cleaning up owner/epoch approach later.

kevin: I'll draft a small change to ResEntry (add reserved u16) and handlers: compactor increments reserved before set_owner, evict checks reserved>0 and defers finalize, compactor decrements after ack. I'll add metrics and a feature flag. Patch will be low-risk.

lia: add e2e perf check to ensure single-token latency doesn't regress. Canary rollout plan: one pool, traffic mirroring with 1% live traffic.

deploybot: deploybot: canary build pushed to pool 'prefetch-canary-3' (build 20260315-57) — CI green, smoke tests passed.

maya: thanks. Sync tomorrow 10:00 to review stress results and decide RFC scope.

kevin: ack, will post patch PR and brief design note in the PR description.

sarah: thanks all.
